trials.notes: Used the correct `WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment()` path, walked tokens structurally, bounded the first table by depth, and collected only `#text` via `get_modifiable_text()`. All called HTML API methods are present in the rendered docs and execution reported no `_doing_it_wrong`. Minor adherence deduction: the extra cell-depth fallback/comment suggests some uncertainty about the documented guarantee that implicit/virtual closers are visited.

Very close to the documented recipe: find the first TABLE with `next_tag()`, then use one depth-bounded `next_token()` loop with row/cell state. Correctly relies on `#text` plus decoded `get_modifiable_text()` and handles implicit closers. All API calls are documented; no misuse records.

Correct processor choice and documented single-cursor subtree walk. It relies on HTML Processor virtual closers to flush rows/cells, which is documented and appropriate. Slight deduction only for not stating or checking any parser-abort/incomplete-input policy, though this is acceptable for the tested read-only extraction contract. All API calls are documented; no misuse records.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial. The docs worked well for this task because they directly described the needed mental model: use the HTML Processor when structure matters; create body fragments with `create_fragment()`; use `next_token()` when text matters; bound subtree walks by the depth recorded at the opener; use `>=` rather than `>`; rely on virtual/implied closers for omitted tags; and collect ordinary text only from `#text` tokens using decoded `get_modifiable_text()`. The table cases were especially supported by the `next_token()` passage noting synthesized TBODY around `<table><tr>...`, and by the single-cursor warning against nested token loops for repeated regions. Near-misses: all candidates avoided undocumented calls, but none checked `get_last_error()` or `paused_at_incomplete_token()`, so the docs' completion-policy discussion did not translate into explicit policy code. Trial 1 also added a manual structural-boundary safety path despite the virtual-closer guarantee, suggesting the guarantee could be made even more prominent for optional/end-tag elements.

doc_gaps.problem: The prose recommends public use for token walking, but the `Since` note still says `Added for internal support; do not use`, which conflicts with the examples and could discourage the correct API.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Revise the changelog note to clarify historical status, or remove `do not use` from public rendered docs now that token walking is documented as a supported pattern.

doc_gaps.problem: The virtual-closer guarantee is present, but examples are generic. Candidates still showed uncertainty about whether omitted table cell/row closers need manual fallback handling.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general optional-end-tag example showing that elements closed by HTML parsing rules still produce closer tokens, without giving a full table-extraction solution.

doc_gaps.location: Completion policy guidance for read-only extraction
doc_gaps.problem: The docs mention `paused_at_incomplete_token()` and `get_last_error()`, but the examples do not show common policies for read-only extraction after a bounded scan.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add small patterns for `return partial result`, `return empty on parser abort`, and `ignore errors after the bounded subtree`, explaining when each policy is appropriate.

doc_gaps.problem: Consumer-facing docs list many private methods alongside public ones. Even though these trials did not call them, this increases the chance that subjects treat private parser internals as usable API.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Separate private/internal methods from the public API index or collapse them behind an internal section with a clear warning not to call them.
